standard_prerequisites.name: Integrality of a ring map, defined by the existence of a monic polynomial relation with coefficients in the source for every element of the target
standard_prerequisites.use: Provides the polynomial satisfied by the chosen element.

core_obligations: Choose an element of the base changed ring and, using integrality of the original map, find a monic polynomial with coefficients in the source that its image satisfies (proof lines 612-616).
Lift the coefficients of that polynomial to the ring appearing in the fibre product, possible because the structure map is surjective (proof lines 616-618).

Observe that the lifted polynomial relation holds modulo the common kernel and adjust the constant coefficient, using the coincidence of the two kernels, to obtain an honest monic relation in the base changed ring (proof lines 618-619).
proof_roadmap: Produce the monic relation downstairs (proof lines 612-616).
Adjust using the common kernel and conclude (proof lines 618-620).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that in the fibre product situation integrality of one structure map implies integrality of the corresponding base changed map, and the proof is a 9-line elementwise argument using the identification of the two kernels. It takes an element of the base changed ring, writes down the monic polynomial with coefficients in the source that it satisfies thanks to integrality, lifts the coefficients along the surjection from the fibre product of rings, and then observes that the polynomial relation holds modulo the common kernel; because the two kernels coincide, the last coefficient can be adjusted to make the relation an honest equation, which is the integrality statement. The lift of the coefficients and the kernel adjustment are the two steps, and both are displayed.
